edits.text: 1. PURPOSE AND USE. The parties wish to explore a potential transaction (the “Purpose”) and may disclose Confidential Information to one another. The receiving party shall use Confidential Information solely to evaluate, negotiate, or pursue the Purpose, and shall not use it for any other purpose or disclose it except as expressly permitted by this Agreement.

2. CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS. “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed by or on behalf of a party or its representatives, in any form, that is identified as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential in the circumstances. The receiving party shall protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own similar information, and in no event less than reasonable care. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its and its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, financing sources, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties at least as protective as this Agreement. The receiving party is responsible for its representatives’ compliance. These obligations do not apply to information the receiving party can demonstrate was publicly available through no breach of this Agreement, already known to it without a duty of confidentiality, received lawfully from a third party without a duty of confidentiality, or independently developed without use of or reference to Confidential Information.

3. TERM; SURVIVAL. This Agreement remains in effect for twenty-four months from the date of signing. The obligations concerning Confidential Information disclosed during the term survive for three years from the date of each disclosure; provided that trade secrets remain protected for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law.

4. COMPELLED DISCLOSURE; RETURN; REMEDIES. If the receiving party is legally required to disclose Confidential Information, it may do so only to the extent required and, to the extent legally permitted, shall give the disclosing party prompt notice and reasonably cooperate, at the disclosing party’s expense, in seeking confidential treatment. Upon written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy the disclosing party’s Confidential Information, except that it may retain archival copies maintained in accordance with routine backup or legal-compliance procedures, which remain subject to this Agreement. A breach may cause irreparable harm for which damages may be inadequate; the disclosing party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief, in addition to any other available remedies, subject to applicable law.
